name: Transco Dalton Expansion Project

values.Owner: Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company LLC; Southern Company Gas

researcher_notes: This is a separate lateral and not part of the Transco main line row P0271. No Dalton row exists in the roster. The Alabama Georgia Connector (P7805) and Hillabee rows are different projects. Pipeline and Gas Journal reported in July 2017 that all facilities were in service. It describes 115 miles of new steel pipe from Coweta County to Paulding and Murray Counties, Georgia, designed for about 448,000 dekatherms per day. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approval (docket CP15-117) was reported in August 2016, with 16 to 30 inch pipe, construction starting that month. The EIA natural gas pipeline projects table for August 2026 (Historical Projects sheet, Excel row 852) lists 115 miles, 16 inch, 448 million cubic feet per day, completed April 2017, cost 471.9 million dollars. EIA is a single origin and lists only 16 inches, so diameter uses the 16 to 30 inch range from the 2016 and 2017 trade reports. Ownership: the lateral is co-owned by Williams Partners and Southern Company Gas, but the split was not found, so no percentages are given. Owner names were not matched to an existing entity (the lookup returned only fuzzy word hits), so they are written as sources give them in the team style. Parent is Williams Companies Inc and Southern Company by inference. No route research was done; RouteType and RouteAccuracy are left for the routes step. Separate item for the discovery queue: EIA row 36 of the Projects sheet, Dalton Lateral Expansion II Project, a proposed 2029 looping of the same lateral (115 miles, 460 million cubic feet per day, announced); it is not this candidate. Confidence high.
